📡 IRGC says warning fire forced US F-16 away from Iran’s airspace

📌 Tehran, IRNA – The Islamic Revolution Guards Corps (IRGC) has announced that a US F-16 fighter jet changed course and moved away from Iranian airspace after warning fire from an air defense system operated by the IRGC Aerospace Force.

In its statement on Thursday, the IRGC said the aircraft had approached Iranian airspace southeast of Hengam Island in an operation near the Strait of Hormuz, while escorting vessels violating maritime rules and providing them with air cover.
​
The statement said the air defense system fired a warning shot, prompting the fighter to perform a sharp maneuver before turning away from the country’s airspace.
​
The IRGC warned that attempts to circumvent regulations governing maritime traffic in the Strait of Hormuz were unacceptable. It said continued violations could bring heavier losses for the vessels involved and the military forces supporting them.
​
The statement described Iran’s airspace as a red line and warned US commanders that any renewed intrusion by American fighter jets would be met with a decisive air defense response.
​
Such a response, it added, could leave the aircraft facing a fate similar to that of an F-15 fighter and US drones previously targeted.

Good morning from Galilee.

It’s Friday morning here, and this may be the last weekend with Benjamin Netanyahu as prime minister. By next Friday, Israel could have a minority government that survives on the votes of politicians who reject Israel as a Jewish state and praise those who want us dead. The parties seeking to form that government would be breaking the very promises they made to their voters. I believe that would be a fraud on the people who elected them. Unseating Netanyahu seems to trump everything else. “Once he’s gone, we’ll see if what we just did can even work.”

I fear that the gains of the last three years of fighting could be thrown away. Hezbollah, Hamas, and the Islamic Republic will hear the same message: Israel is weak. I can imagine what their leaders would say to one another. “Finally, our nightmare is over. The people who defend us now have leverage over Israel’s government. We can plot quietly and strike again when the time comes.”

Every Israeli conservative has every right to feel sad, angry, and concerned. For many of us, faith in God is what keeps those feelings from turning into despair. We answer to an authority higher than the government or the Supreme Court. We know how strong the IDF is, and we know that God is stronger.

As for me, I feel torn.

I want to believe that things will turn around. Yet when I read the Word of God, I see a war still ahead. I see the Lord fighting for Israel and giving us victory. I also see the deception that follows, when people rush to welcome a world leader who will present himself as the savior of the world.

The book of Revelation gives us a picture of what is coming upon the world. As for Israel, Zechariah tells us that two-thirds will perish. Scripture promises that Israel will experience salvation as a nation, and it tells us how much of our own people will perish before that day. I find it hard to even write those words.

When the Lord called me to this teaching ministry, He called me to teach you what His Word says about Israel’s present and future. I want you to pray for my people and carry a burden to share with them the good news of Yeshua the Messiah. He was, is, and always will be their only hope.

Yes, I will always take joy in seeing our enemies defeated. My greatest joy will be to see my nation saved.

Paul wrote in Romans 9:1–5:

“I tell the truth in Christ, I am not lying, my conscience also bearing me witness in the Holy Spirit, that I have great sorrow and continual grief in my heart. For I could wish that I myself were accursed from Christ for my brethren, my countrymen according to the flesh, who are Israelites, to whom pertain the adoption, the glory, the covenants, the giving of the law, the service of God, and the promises; of whom are the fathers and from whom, according to the flesh, Christ came, who is over all, the eternally blessed God. Amen.”

Paul was beaten and driven out of towns by some of his own countrymen who rejected his message. And still, he could say he would bear the curse himself for their sake. I don’t know if I could have said those words.

Israel is God’s irreplaceable people. We are also far from perfect. Our embrace of liberalism and globalism, our tolerance of Islamism, and above all our rejection of the Messiah will have consequences. By next Friday, we may be seeing the beginning of a painful new chapter.

Today I feel a little of what Paul described to the Corinthians: “hard-pressed on every side, yet not crushed; perplexed, but not in despair.”

I look around and see politicians so determined to remove Netanyahu that they are willing to give a small, radical minority the power to decide whether their government stands or falls. That grieves me deeply. Whatever happens next Friday, I will keep teaching what God’s Word says about my nation, and I will keep praying for my people.

Have a blessed weekend.

Awaiting His Soon Return,

Amir

🖥 Army ground force ready to defend Iran’s borders: Deputy cmdr.

📌 Tehran, IRNA – Brigadier General Sirous Amanollahi, deputy commander of the Iranian Army’s Ground Force for operations, says the force is at its highest level of combat readiness and had prepared plans to counter threats.

Speaking to IRNA on Friday, Amanollahi said Ground Force units were deployed along Iran’s borders, from the northwest to the junction of Iran, Turkmenistan and Afghanistan, in line with orders from the Armed Forces General Staff and Army command.
​
He said approved plans had been drawn up based on assessments of adversaries’ capabilities, with combat capacity expanded across the depth and breadth of border areas.
​
Amanollahi said coordination among the Army, the Islamic Revolution Guards Corps, Law Enforcement Force, Basij and popular forces, under the commander-in-chief’s leadership, had strengthened preparedness. Inspections and assessments, he added, showed combat capability was in excellent condition.
​
The military official also said units had received the state-of-the-art weapons and equipment, including air defense and maneuver systems, and were ready to respond under existing plans.
​
He said Iran’s experience in the eight-year war imposed by the Iraqi Ba’athist regime, as well as in recent conflicts involving the United States and the Israeli regime, had shaped its military preparations.
​
Amanollahi said the military would resist any attempt to threaten Iran’s borders and would not allow hostile forces to enter the country. He attributed the prevention of ground operations to public presence.
